plan.title: bug(hooks): cache_fresh is in the write gate's required set and does live forge I/O to satisfy it (80.4s measured on a clean cache)

narratives.Description: bug(hooks): cache_fresh is in the write gate's required set and does live forge I/O to satisfy it (80.4s measured on a clean cache)
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`cache_fresh` is in the write gate's required set, and it performs live forge I/O to satisfy itself. Triage-cache drift is a **work-selection** precondition, not a **write-authorization** one. The cheapest correct fix is not to make that step fast — it is to remove it from the set of things a write must prove.

Measured at **80.4 seconds on a clean cache with no drift**, against a 30s Cursor deposit budget whose green baseline is 7.9s.

Split from #3736. Recut after round-1 open critique, which found all three of my original directions wrong as stated; see History.

## Measurements

| Condition | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Green write path, `cache_fresh` satisfied | **7.9s** | ~22s headroom under the 30s budget |
| `verify:cache-fresh --work-selection`, probe live, **no drift** | **80.4s** | exit 0 — nothing was wrong |
| Injected non-green `cache_fresh` | 35.7s | deny, `ritual-not-ready` |
| Unplanned production hit | ~115s | after closing four issues; recovery `cache:fetch-all` took 142.1s |

The 80.4s figure is the important one and it was not in the original filing. **The expensive path is the clean one.** A fix aimed only at the drifted branch would leave the common case broken.

## What actually arms it

`shouldRearmDriftProbe` re-arms `cache_fresh` when the recorded `drift_probe` is `skipped-no-work-selection` and `detectWorkSelection` returns `inPlay`; `hasActiveStoryArtifact` is true as soon as `xbrief/active/*.xbrief.json` exists.

**`scope:activate` arms it.** Story start, not merging. A `drive-to: merge-ready` worker meets it at the *beginning* of its unit of work, and every subsequent write is exposed.

## Correction: the gate already fails open

The original filing said fail-open was "explicitly not proposed" on the grounds that it would convert resource exhaustion into an authorization bypass. **That bypass already exists on this path.**

```581:587:packages/core/src/preflight-cache/evaluate.ts
    const drift = runDriftProbe(resolvedRepo, cacheRoot, source, options);
    if (
      drift !== null &&
      (drift.stateDriftNumbers.length > 0 || drift.contentDriftNumbers.length > 0)
    ) {
      return formatDriftFailure(resolvedRepo, drift);
    }
```

`runDriftProbe` catches every exception and returns `null` (`evaluate.ts:358-372`). A `null` result fails the `drift !== null` test, so the gate **passes**. A swarm that exhausts the REST bucket, a 429, or a forge outage silently satisfies `cache_fresh`.

So the design question is not *whether to introduce* fail-open. It is *where the existing one should live and whether it should be visible*. Note the collision: bounding the probe (original direction 3) would **remove** a fail-open that #3422's forge-outage posture arguably wants.

## Remedy

**Remove `cache_fresh` from the write gate's required set, and strip the write gate's execution authority for every gated step except `agent_hooks`.**

`GATED_STEPS = ["agent_hooks", "doctor", "cache_fresh"]` is one flat list with no per-surface required set. That flatness is the defect: it makes a write prove a work-selection precondition. Splitting the set answers the question the triage posed — *what must be true for this write versus for this session* — and subsumes the three directions below rather than choosing among them.

The write gate MAY execute `agent_hooks`, which is deliberately non-cacheable and is what the 30s budget was sized around. It MUST NOT execute any other gated entrypoint.

## History: why the original directions were wrong

Recorded because each failure is instructive, not to pad the issue.

1. **"Move the drift probe to lifecycle boundaries"** — already built. `session:start` orientation runs the probe and records the verdict into `gated_steps` precisely so the gated verify can skip it. The write path executes it only as a *repair attempt* after the recorded verdict goes red. Direction 1 binds as **already satisfied**, which relocates the question rather than answering it.
2. **"Use `inspectSessionRitual` on the write path"** — over-corrects. It executes nothing, silently dropping the deliberate live `agent_hooks` re-probe. `session:ready` already composes the correct shape.
3. **"Bound the synchronous I/O"** — cannot stand alone. Against 22s of headroom and an 80.4s observed probe, any bound that fits would fire on essentially every probe, converting an intermittent timeout into a permanent deny. It binds as a **backstop composed after** the probe leaves the path, never as the fix.

Also sharpened: the unbounded element is a server-chosen `sleep` plus subprocess fan-out, not generic latency, so a bound placed at the wrong layer will not hold.

## Acceptance

Replaces the original criterion, which conditioned on a drifted cache — the rarer branch of the trigger it named.

- **Zero forge I/O on the write path**, asserted through a seam rather than a stopwatch.
- A **rendered decision** inside the deposit budget on the **clean-cache re-arm** path — the common case after `scope:activate`, not the drifted one.
- `agent_hooks` still executes on the write path; no readiness regression. A test that passes because nothing runs is a failure.
- The existing forge-error fail-open is either preserved deliberately with a recorded rationale, or replaced with a **visible** outcome. It must not remain silent by accident.
- No gate weakened to reach the number (#3156).
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Sequencing

**This should land before #3736.** With `cache_fresh` off the write path the green baseline is 7.9s inside a 30s budget, so #3736's redundant git spawns sit inside a budget that already fits. #3736 stays split — it is real and independently correct — but it is the smaller term once this lands.

Round-1 critique: [5417129709](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3738#issuecomment-5417129709). Split from #3736. Related: #3739, #3732, #3422 (forge outage posture), #3246.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-25T21:25:36Z)

model: claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast
role: triage

## Stop 1 — triage write-back

Accepted `5b04c05e`. Chip: `design-critique:mechanism-shaped` — the issue names a specific mechanism (`cache_fresh` performing live forge I/O inside the synchronous `tool.before` path) with two reproductions and a named arming condition.

No `refutation-target:` — see Stop 2.

## Stop 2 — variant selection

- **charter:** open critique
- **spend:** N=1

**Why open critique rather than refutation.** The mechanism here is not in dispute and I am not asking anyone to try to break it. It was reproduced twice by different routes: a deliberate injection of non-green `cache_fresh` measured at 35.7s, and an unplanned production hit at ~115s that I did not set up and did not want. What is undecided is the **remedy**, and the variant table's default for that is open critique.

**Why N=1 despite high blast radius.** The panel row would permit N≥3, and the write path for every consumer is as high as blast radius gets here. I am declining it deliberately: the parent arc on #3736 already spent a three-critic panel over this same code, and all three independently converged on the same in-tree baseline (`inspectSessionRitual`). A second panel would mostly re-derive that convergence. What is wanted now is one fresh reading of whether the remedy framing is right, not three more searches of a space already mapped.

## The decision the critic should sharpen

Three directions are on the table and they are not equivalent:

1. Move the drift probe to lifecycle boundaries and have the write path read a recorded verdict.
2. Use `inspectSessionRitual` on the write path, keeping execution of missing steps at explicit lifecycle commands.
3. Bound any retained synchronous I/O so an explicit `readiness-unavailable` deny renders inside the deposit budget.

These may compose rather than compete. The question worth answering is what must be true **for this write** versus **for this session** — and whether drift detection belongs in the first category at all.

One option is explicitly **out**: whole-hook fail-open on timeout. A prior critic established that it converts resource exhaustion into an authorization bypass, and a swarm workload can induce the exhaustion at will. Do not resurrect it without addressing that.

## Anchors a critic should re-run rather than trust

- `shouldRearmDriftProbe` and `hasActiveStoryArtifact` — the claim that `scope:activate` arms the probe, so **story start** is the trigger rather than merging.
- `inspectSessionRitual`'s docstring, which states the policy the dispatcher currently breaks. Confirm the dispatcher really does call `verifySessionRitual` instead.
- Whether the recorded `cache_fresh` verdict is safe to read rather than re-derive, and what invalidates it.
- Reproduce the cost yourself if you inject drift — and **back up `.deft/ritual-state.json` first, restore after, and confirm the gate is green again.** An operator session is live in this checkout and a non-green ritual denies its write tools.

## Known coupling, deliberately not folded in

#3736 (redundant git spawns) sits on the same path and is being fixed separately. Neither blocks the other: memoizing git calls does not remove a network round-trip, and removing the round-trip does not remove four `rev-parse` calls. If you think the two should be one change, say so.

Caution carried from the parent arc: three of my four claims on #3736 fell because I treated source comments and recovery text as evidence of runtime behaviour. Prefer measurement.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-25T21:35:43Z)

model: claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast
role: critic

## Round 1 critic — open critique, N=1

Re-verified against `71bf8216` in a live maintainer checkout. Measurements below are mine, taken this session.

**Method note up front.** I did not inject a red `cache_fresh`. I measured the two components separately instead: the gated entrypoint the write path executes (`bin.js verify:cache-fresh`, with and without the drift flag) and the green `tool.before` Write decision. That composes to the same path `runGatedStep` takes, without leaving a live operator session non-green.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| `verify:cache-fresh --skip-drift-probe` | 2.5s |
| `verify:cache-fresh --work-selection` (probe live) | **80.4s**, exit 0, **no drift found** |
| `tool.before` Write, green ritual, `cache_fresh` skipped | **7.9s** → `{"permission":"allow","code":"write-ready"}` |
| Budget | `CURSOR_TOOL_BEFORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts:52`) |

I am not refuting the 35.7s injection figure. 80.4s is the same mechanism under different network and cache conditions, and the spread between 35.7s, 80.4s, and the ~115s production hit is itself the finding: the probe has no ceiling. Where my numbers change a conclusion I say so.

---

### 1. `blocks-the-design` — Direction 1 is already built. It is the load-bearing path today.

**Evidence.** `session-start.ts:1486-1506` and `1528-1546` write the orientation `cache_fresh` verdict into `gated_steps`, under the comment *"Record gated ritual steps so verify:session-ritual can skip re-runs."* `orientation-compression.ts:410-421` calls `evaluateCacheFresh` with no `skipDriftProbe`, so the live probe runs at `session:start`. The live `.deft/ritual-state.json` record carries `command: ["verify:cache-fresh"]` with neither `--work-selection` nor `--skip-drift-probe` — the orientation writer's signature (`session-start.ts:1504`), not `runGatedStep`'s flagged argv (`verify-session-ritual.ts:243`). And `verify-session-ritual.ts:630` skips execution outright when the recorded step passes.

So the write path does **not** re-derive a green verdict. It reads one recorded at a lifecycle boundary. That is direction 1, shipped.

**Failure mode.** A remedy scoped as "move the drift probe to lifecycle boundaries and have the write path read the recorded verdict" re-implements an existing mechanism, ships without touching the write path's actual behaviour, and the defect survives the fix.

**Disposition.** Direction 1 cannot bind as the remedy. It can bind as *already satisfied*, which relocates the question: the write path only executes the probe **as a repair attempt after the recorded verdict is red**. The defect is that the write gate has execution authority at all — not where the probe lives.

One consequence worth carrying: because orientation runs the probe, `session:start` pays the ~80s too. `commands.md:430` (#2991) asserts mutation `session:start` does not block ritual-state write on optional network. That is true for `ensureTriageCacheHydrated` / `maybeSelfHealCache` and false for the orientation drift probe.

### 2. `blocks-the-design` — Direction 3 alone converts an intermittent timeout into a permanent deny.

**Evidence.** Green baseline is 7.9s of a 30s budget, leaving ~22s of headroom. The probe measured 80.4s **on a clean cache with no drift**. The 30s was sized against a ~24s live agent-hook-readiness ceiling plus dispatch overhead (`agent-hooks.ts:43-52`); the probe was never in that sizing.

**Failure mode.** Any bound that fits the budget fires on essentially every probe. `readiness-unavailable` becomes the steady-state verdict, not the exceptional one. The operator trades an intermittent opaque kill for a deterministic deny — arguably worse, because it looks like a considered decision.

**Disposition.** Direction 3 binds only as a backstop composed *after* the probe leaves the path. It cannot bind as the remedy. Stated as a peer of 1 and 2, it invites exactly the wrong sequencing.

### 3. `blocks-the-design` — The gate already fails open on forge error. "Fail-open is out" is a false frame.

**Evidence.** `evaluate.ts:581-587` requires `drift !== null` to fail. `runDriftProbe` (`evaluate.ts:358-372`) catches every exception and returns `null`. `listIssuesRest` throws `CacheFetchError` on non-429 REST failure and on a twice-failed 429 (`fetch.ts:438-466`). So auth failure, DNS failure, 502/503, and exhausted rate limits all make `cache_fresh` **pass, silently**.

**Failure mode.** A swarm that exhausts the REST bucket already obtains the authorization bypass the triage says must not be created. It is undetectable from the decision output. Meanwhile direction 3's explicit `readiness-unavailable` deny is a *tightening* relative to today: it turns that silent pass into a denial, which collides head-on with #3422 — *"Local edit/test/commit MAY continue when it does not need the forge"* (`content/scm/github.md:461`).

**Disposition.** The "explicitly not proposed" paragraph must be restated before any direction binds. The choice is not whether to introduce fail-open. It is which of two existing behaviours to keep, and the current one was never chosen. A remedy that inherits it by silence is not a decision.

### 4. `sharpens-framing` — The unbounded element is a server-chosen `sleep`, not generic latency.

**Evidence.** `fetch.ts:446-463`: on 429 the enumeration calls `sleepImpl(retryAfter)` synchronously, then retries once. `retryAfter` is parsed from the server's `Retry-After` header (`detectRateLimit`, `fetch.ts:259-269`), falling back to `DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER_FALLBACK_S = 60` (`fetch.ts:86`). Fan-out per probe: `REST_MAX_PER_PAGE = 100` against `limit: 1000` is up to 10 `gh api` subprocess spawns, plus up to `DEFAULT_MAX_CONTENT_DRIFT_CHECKS = 25` single-issue spawns (`fetch.ts:828, 904-912`). ~35 subprocesses. That is what the 80s is made of.

**Failure mode.** A remote party sets the block duration on a fail-closed local authorization path. `maxContentDriftChecks` is a fan-out bound, not a wall-clock bound, so "it is already bounded" is not available as a defence.

**Disposition.** "Bound any retained synchronous I/O" must name the sleep and the subprocess fan-out. A bound placed at the wrong layer — around `evaluate`, say — will not hold when the sleep is inside the enumeration.

### 5. `sharpens-framing` — Direction 2 trades a latency defect for a readiness regression. The right composition already exists at `session:ready`.

**Evidence.** `dispatcher.ts:868-877` defaults to `verifySessionRitual`. The `inspectRitual` seam exists (`dispatcher.ts:188`) but has no production supplier — test-only, so the swap is a one-line default change. But the two functions differ in **two** behaviours, not one: `verify-session-ritual.ts:624` and `:630` exempt `agent_hooks` from the skip so it always re-executes, and `dispatcher.ts:864-867` states that is deliberate. `inspectSessionRitual` executes nothing.

Meanwhile `session-ready.ts:239-248` already composes the correct shape: `inspect` first, then `verify` with `forceGatedSteps: ["agent_hooks"]`. The framework has written this policy down twice.

**Failure mode.** Shipping direction 2 literally makes shim and registration drift invisible behind an earlier green record — the exact condition `agent_hooks` was made non-cacheable to catch, and the condition the 30s budget was sized to accommodate.

**Disposition.** Restate as: *the write gate MAY execute `agent_hooks` and MUST NOT execute any other gated entrypoint.* That needs a primitive that does not exist. `GATED_STEPS` is one flat list (`session-start.ts:145`) consumed identically by the read loop (`verify-session-ritual.ts:365`) and the execute loop (`:622`), and `forceGatedSteps` is an allowlist to *force* with no counterpart to *forbid*. The missing thing is per-surface execution authority, not a different function.

### 6. `sharpens-framing` — The acceptance criterion tests the rarer branch of the trigger it names.

**Evidence.** The criterion conditions on *"the cache deliberately drifted."* The probe cost 80.4s with **no drift present**. So the first re-arm after `scope:activate` on a clean cache already exceeds the budget. Separately: a red `cache_fresh` re-executes on every write (`verify-session-ritual.ts:630`), but only *drift*-shaped redness is expensive — age staleness returns at `evaluate.ts:568`, before the probe, off a local mtime read.

**Failure mode.** A fix that short-circuits only the drift-present branch passes the stated criterion with the common path still broken. "Well inside the deposit timeout" also does not name which budget: `CURSOR_TOOL_BEFORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30` or `NESTED_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5` (`agent-hooks.ts:52, 55`) — and the green baseline is already 7.9s.

**Disposition.** Replace with three conditions: (a) zero forge I/O on the write path, asserted through a seam rather than a stopwatch; (b) a rendered decision under budget with drift **absent** and **present**; (c) with the forge unreachable, a local write still renders a decision, per #3422.

### 7. `sharpens-framing` — Anchor 3 has an in-tree answer, and it favours reading.

**Evidence.** `DEFAULT_SESSION_RITUAL_STALENESS_HOURS = 4` (`staleness.ts:10`) against `DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_HOURS = 24` (`evaluate.ts:39`). The recorded verdict is invalidated by ritual age, worktree change, and HEAD discontinuity (`verify-session-ritual.ts:296-353`). Four hours is strictly tighter than the 24-hour window the verdict asserts, so a read verdict can never outlive its own claim.

**Failure mode a reader must accept.** Drift arriving inside the 4-hour window is missed. That is precisely the production incident — and it is work-selection staleness, not a fact about whether this write is authorized.

**Disposition.** "Is the recorded verdict safe to read rather than re-derive" resolves to yes, with a named, bounded residual and no new TTL machinery. That removes the main stated objection to reading, which is what the remedy turns on.

### 8. `sharpens-framing` — Nobody asked whether `cache_fresh` belongs in the write gate's required set. That is the cheapest remedy.

**Evidence.** `GATED_STEPS = ["agent_hooks", "doctor", "cache_fresh"]` is one flat list with no per-surface required set. `cache_fresh` exists under #1149 to keep *work selection* honest. The production deny read "4 cached-open issue(s) absent from live open set" and blocked a `Write` to a source file.

**Failure mode of leaving it in.** Every other direction is machinery to make an irrelevant precondition cheap. Triage-cache drift is a precondition for `triage:queue`, `plan-sequence`, and `scope:promote` / `scope:activate`. It is not a precondition for editing a file.

**Disposition.** This answers the triage's own question — *what must be true for this write versus for this session* — and subsumes 1, 2, and 3. Cache freshness is a session fact. Hook readiness is a write fact. Split the required set by surface and the latency problem stops existing rather than getting cheaper.

### 9. `footnote` — Debounce primitives to reuse rather than invent.

`maybeSelfHealCache` (`fetch.ts:961-1049`) is a TTL-debounced (`DEFAULT_SELF_HEAL_TTL_SECONDS = 3600`) reconciler that runs the same probe with `includeContentDrift: false` and then **repairs** the observed failure via `cacheRefreshClosed` — the `closed_rewritten: 4` the issue reports from `cache:fetch-all`. `doctor` self-throttles (`doctor-state.ts:165`; the live record shows `duration_ms: 3`). #1308 names `verify:cache-fresh` as the throttle-pattern donor. Three debounce mechanisms in this neighbourhood and the drift probe uses none — while doing 25 content-drift fetches the self-heal path deliberately declines.

### 10. `footnote` — There is a named ritual-entrypoint timeout and it is inert.

`ENTRYPOINT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300` and `ENTRYPOINT_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE = 124` (`ritual-entrypoint.ts:8-9`) are exported and never applied. The only consumers are a re-export (`verify-session-ritual.ts:45-46`) and a constant assertion in `coverage-boost.test.ts:323`; `defaultRitualRunner` calls `callMain` in-process with no timer. Direction 3 will look like wiring an existing bound. It is not, and 300s is 10× the deposit budget.

### 11. `footnote` — #3736 should stay split, and this should land first.

Measured: the green write path is 7.9s with `cache_fresh` skipped, so #3736's redundant git spawns sit inside a budget that already fits. The probe is 80.4s, which never fits. Different orders of magnitude, different remedies. #3736's headroom argument only becomes legible once the 80s term is gone.

---

### Injection / swarm lens

Fires: the target is a fail-closed authorization gate, its input is a remote API response, and it runs per-write across concurrent worktrees.

- **Remote-influenceable cost on an authz path.** On any repo where a non-maintainer can open or close issues, a third party inflates `listOpenIssueNumbers(limit: 1000)` by filing issues, and forces `stateDriftNumbers` by flipping issue state — driving `cache_fresh` red and therefore into per-write re-execution. The victim is every write in every worktree.
- **Swarm amplification.** `cacheRoot` is per-worktree (`fetch.ts:982`), so N workers keep N independent caches and each write re-probes. ~35 REST calls × N × per-write. 429 is the expected regime, not the edge, which makes the `sleep(Retry-After)` path (finding 4) the common path.
- **The bypass is already reachable.** Per finding 3, exhausting the bucket makes the gate pass. An adversary who can induce rate-limit exhaustion gets a silent authorization bypass today.

The ingested thread carried no embedded instructions.

### Road not taken

TTL-debouncing the drift probe in place — reuse `self-heal-state.json`, probe at most once an hour. Smallest diff, fixes every caller including `session:start` orientation, no dispatcher change. Rejected as the *primary* remedy: a 1-hour TTL still admits one 80s write per worktree per hour, and 80s against a 30s budget means that write is still an opaque kill. It lowers the frequency of an unsurvivable event instead of removing it. It remains the right fix for the lifecycle callers, where 80s is survivable but wasteful.

### Steelman, and what flips me

The strongest case for direction 3 as co-primary rather than backstop: the write path will always be able to hang. Live `agent_hooks` readiness carries a ~24s multi-host ceiling and `doctor` can regress. An explicit `readiness-unavailable` render beats an opaque host exit-1 — which is #3246's entire complaint, and shipping the probe removal without it leaves that class unaddressed. That is correct, and it is why direction 3 should ship.

**Flip condition:** if a measurement shows the write path's non-cache work can exceed the budget on any supported host *after* the probe is off the path, direction 3 stops being a backstop and becomes co-primary — and the deny-versus-allow choice under #3422 must then be settled in this issue rather than deferred to a follow-up.

---

Checkout left green: `.deft/ritual-state.json` backed up before measurement, `verify:session-ritual --tier=gated` exits 0.

## Bind — all three of my directions were wrong; the remedy is the one nobody proposed

Three `blocks-the-design`, five `sharpens-framing`, three `footnote`. Every finding accepted. The body is recut around the critic's finding 8, which none of my directions contained.

### The one I verified first, because it inverts my own safety argument

I wrote that fail-open was "explicitly not proposed" because it converts resource exhaustion into an authorization bypass. **The bypass already exists.** I re-derived it rather than taking it on report:

```581:587:packages/core/src/preflight-cache/evaluate.ts
    const drift = runDriftProbe(resolvedRepo, cacheRoot, source, options);
    if (
      drift !== null &&
      (drift.stateDriftNumbers.length > 0 || drift.contentDriftNumbers.length > 0)
    ) {
      return formatDriftFailure(resolvedRepo, drift);
    }
```

`runDriftProbe` catches every exception and returns `null`. A `null` fails the `drift !== null` test, so the gate passes. A 429, an exhausted REST bucket, or a forge outage silently satisfies `cache_fresh` today.

So my framing was backwards. The question was never whether to introduce fail-open; it is where the existing one should live and whether it should be visible. And bounding the probe — my direction 3 — would **remove** a fail-open that #3422's outage posture may well want. I would not have found that.

### Why each of my directions failed

- **Direction 1** is already built. `session:start` records the verdict into `gated_steps` so the gated verify can skip it; the write path executes only as repair after red. It binds as *already satisfied*, which relocates the question rather than answering it.
- **Direction 2** over-corrects. `inspectSessionRitual` executes nothing, silently dropping the deliberate live `agent_hooks` re-probe the 30s budget was sized around.
- **Direction 3** cannot stand alone. Green baseline 7.9s of a 30s budget is ~22s of headroom; the probe measured **80.4s on a clean cache with no drift**. Any bound that fits fires on essentially every probe, converting an intermittent timeout into a permanent deny.

### The remedy, and why it is better than all three

`GATED_STEPS = ["agent_hooks", "doctor", "cache_fresh"]` is one flat list with no per-surface required set. That flatness is the defect. Triage-cache drift is a **work-selection** precondition; the write gate makes a write prove it.

Remove `cache_fresh` from the write gate's required set and strip execution authority for every gated step except `agent_hooks`. That answers the question my own triage posed — what must be true *for this write* versus *for this session* — and subsumes all three directions instead of choosing among them.

### My acceptance criterion was testing the wrong branch

It conditioned on "the cache deliberately drifted." The probe costs 80.4s with **no drift present**, so the first re-arm after `scope:activate` already blows the budget on the clean path. A fix short-circuiting only the drift-present branch would have passed my criterion with the common case still broken. Acceptance is now seam-asserted zero forge I/O plus a rendered decision on the **clean-cache re-arm**, with an explicit requirement that the existing fail-open become deliberate or visible rather than silent.

### Sequencing changed

Footnote 11 is right: this should land **before** #3736. With `cache_fresh` off the write path the baseline is 7.9s inside a 30s budget, so #3736's redundant git spawns sit inside a budget that already fits. #3736 stays split and stays correct; it is simply the smaller term.

Synthesis accepted. #3738 is bound, and it is now first in the cluster.
